QUOTE: "Without `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS`, it expands to `private_##member`... Code that writes `ctx->foo` compiles only when the define is set... an application that reads `ctx->foo` gets "no member named foo"... It is a naming barrier, not access control. Anyone can write `ctx->private_foo`"
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says the opacity is enforced at compile time by mangling the member name (a naming barrier), and that anyone can still write `ctx->private_foo`, so the fields stay visible and accessible.
